Summary: A community meeting was conducted with site management committee members and IDPs to discuss and identify their main needs and priorities at the site.

Primary Activity: Two-Way Information Sharing, Feedback and Complaints
Summary: An awareness session was conducted on NRC’s Community Feedback Mechanism (CFM). Participants were informed about what can be shared (complaints, feedback, suggestions, enquiries, requests for assistance and thanks) and the available channels: SMS and WhatsApp (0599030327), email (ps.communicate@nrc.no), the QR code on the contact card, feedback boxes at NRC offices, and NRC staff in the office or field. The session stressed that submitting feedback is free and confidential and does not affect access to assistance, and that messages are registered and referred to the relevant team, although registration does not guarantee assistance. Participants were advised to report sensitive complaints (requests for money or favors, exploitation, abuse or harassment) confidentially rather than in public WhatsApp groups. The role of site committees in helping older persons and residents without phones was explained, noting that committees do not replace the mechanism and residents may contact NRC directly.

Primary Activity: Two-Way Information Sharing, Feedback and Complaints
Summary: An awareness session was conducted on winterization and flood preparedness. Participants worked together on a site map to identify tent locations, pathways and the areas where rainwater collects, and discussed practical measures to reduce flooding, such as digging small drainage channels around tents, raising tent floors with sand where available, placing sandbags at tent entrances, and keeping pathways and drainage routes clear. The session covered preparing tents before the rain, including raising mattresses off the ground, protecting documents in nylon bags, keeping the driest area for children and older persons, and reporting worn tents to the site committee. Emergency preparedness was also discussed, including a ready bag with medicines, documents and children’s clothes, and an agreed safer place or host family in case of flooding. Participants were advised on protecting children during and after the rain, covering drinking water, and watching for diarrhoea, fever and signs of severe cold. Safe heating practices were explained, including lighting fires outside tents, ventilation, avoiding burning plastic and recognising carbon monoxide symptoms. Participants were also warned about the hazards of open soak-away pits and standing water, and advised to report flooded areas or open pits to the site committee for referral.

Summary:
بتاريخ 05/11/2026، نُفّذت دورة تدريبية في موقع [الرحمة] استهدفت اللجنة الرئيسية واللجان الفرعية، بما فيها [لجنة المياه والصرف الصحي- التوزيع- الحماية- المرأة والطفل- التعليمية - الصحية]. هدفت الدورة إلى تعزيز فهم المشاركين لمفهوم إدارة المواقع ووظائفها، وتوضيح أدوار الإدارة واللجان ومسؤولياتها، وتعزيز الحماية والمشاركة المجتمعية، والتعريف بآلية الشكاوى والتغذية الراجعة، إضافة إلى إعداد خطة للطوارئ وإدارة الأزمات.
شارك في الدورة 20 شخصاً، منهم 12 ذكور، بينهم شخص فوق 60 عاماً، و8 إناث، ولم يُسجَّل مشاركون من ذوي الإعاقة. وأُجري اختبار قبلي وآخر بعدي لجميع المشاركين لقياس التغيّر في مستوى المعرفة. بلغت مدة الدورة [2] ساعة.

Safety Findings
The assessment highlighted fire safety concerns following previous fire incidents at the site, particularly as some residents continue to cook inside their shelters. The site lacks communal lighting and adequate drainage. Two toilets are not functioning, waste collection remains insufficient, and several shelters provide limited privacy. One person was reported to have been affected by explosive ordnance, although no explosive ordnance was observed within the site during the assessment.
Accessibility Findings
Access to water remains a significant concern. Two water points are out of service, no accessible water point is available, and residents are required to pay a fee to collect water. Although the nearest health facility is less than 30 minutes away on foot, access to healthcare remains challenging. The site also lacks mobile health services, private consultation spaces for women, nearby nutrition services for pregnant and breastfeeding women, and a designated safe space for women and girls.
Recommendations
Immediate attention should be given to identifying safer cooking areas, maintaining clear evacuation routes, and installing lighting along main pathways. The two non-functioning toilets and water points should be repaired, and arrangements should be made to ensure water access for households unable to afford the collection fee. Improvements to drainage and waste collection are also needed, alongside coordination with relevant service providers to address healthcare, nutrition, and protection needs.

Safety Findings
The assessment identified several safety concerns at Nablus Site, including the absence of communal lighting, drainage, and proper waste management. Toilets and bathing facilities were found to be unsafe, while several shelters lacked sufficient privacy and internal locks. Fire safety measures around the cooking area also need improvement. In addition, cases of children working to support their families were reported.
Accessibility Findings
Movement within the site is difficult due to narrow spaces between shelters and the lack of suitable pathways, particularly for older persons and persons with disabilities. There is no accessible water point, and the nearest health facility and market are approximately 30–60 minutes away on foot. Mobile health services and private consultation spaces for women are also unavailable.
Recommendations
Priority should be given to installing solar lighting at entrances and along routes leading to sanitation facilities, improving internal pathways, and establishing an accessible water point. Drainage, waste collection, and privacy measures should also be improved. Coordination with health providers is needed to facilitate access to medical services, while reported child labour cases should be referred confidentially through appropriate child protection channels.

During the women's session, discussions focused on the risks of sexual exploitation and abuse, women's rights to receive humanitarian assistance without any form of payment or exploitation, and the importance of reporting violations through safe and confidential complaint mechanisms. Participants also raised concerns about fear of reporting, psychological and social pressures, particularly among widows, and the need for continued psychosocial support.

During the men's session, discussions highlighted the main challenges facing the camp, particularly the risk of flooding due to its low geographical location, the need for sand barriers to protect tents, and the shortage of shelter materials such as tents and tarpaulins. Participants also highlighted the lack of employment opportunities for young people and the need for a dedicated administrative tent to facilitate community communication, receive feedback and complaints, and organize awareness and social activities. The discussions emphasized the importance of improving protection measures, addressing community needs, and strengthening safe and accessible feedback and reporting mechanisms.

Topic: Community to Site Management Committee Interface Meetings
Summary:
تم عقد اجتماع اللجنة بتاريخ 6\9 وذلك لمناقشة الانجازات والتحديات التى تواجههم وقد أسفر الاجتماع الى التالى :
•	البناء على النجاح: توثيق آلية عمل اللجنة في التنسيق مع البلدية والجهات المحلية (رصد، تصعيد، متابعة، توثيق النتيجة) كنموذج عمل معتمد لتكراره في القطاعات الأخرى، وإتاحته لتبادل الخبرات مع لجان المواقع الأخرى.
•	الاستعداد للشتاء: اعتبار صيانة الخيام والشوادر والإنارة الأولوية الأولى للشهر القادم، مع جدول زمني واضح ومسؤول عن كل خطوة (الحصر، الطلب، التواصل مع الداعمين، التنفيذ التطوعي).
•	التنظيم الداخلي: اعتماد اللجان الفرعية وسجل الشركاء وجدول البلدية الدوري والتقرير الشهري كأدوات دائمة لعمل اللجنة.
•	تعزيز التواصل: الاتفاق على تعزيز التواصل المنتظم والتشاور المستمر بين لجنة إدارة الموقع، فريق المشروع، والسكان.
•	تفعيل الشكاوى والحماية: تفعيل آلية واضحة وآمنة لاستقبال الملاحظات والشكاوى وإحالتها مع الحفاظ التام على السرية، وضمان عدالة الاستهداف في جميع التوزيعات.
•	الرصد والمتابعة الميدانية: تنفيذ رصد ميداني دوري يغطي النظافة، الصرف الصحي، القوارض، صلاحية الخيام، وسلامة الحركة، مع ربط نتائجه بسجل متابعة التحديات.
•	الشمولية والنوع الاجتماعي: تعزيز مشاركة النساء في عمل اللجنة نظراً لمحدودية تمثيلهن الحالي، وضمان مشاركة الفئات المهمشة (الفتيات المراهقات، السيدات المسنات، كبار السن، ذوي الإعاقة) في اللجان الفرعية والنقاشات واتخاذ القرار.

Primary Activity: Two-Way Information Sharing, Feedback and Complaints
Topic(s): PSEA (Protection against Sexual Exploitation & Abuse), General Protection
Summary:
An awareness session was held at Al-Baraa Site (DEB3658) on Monday, 9 November 2026, from 10:10 to 11:10 a.m., with 22 displaced women residing at the site in attendance.

The session covered key protection principles, including dignity, non-discrimination, confidentiality, and access to support services. It also addressed Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA), including prohibited conduct and how to report concerns safely and confidentially.

Under Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP), participants learned about their right to access information and how to use complaints and feedback channels, including the Sanad Network and the channels managed by Faris Al-Arab. The session also covered the role of monitoring and evaluation in gathering residents’ feedback on services, how to inquire about relief assistance, and the criteria used to prioritize groups with the greatest needs.

Challenges/
The discussions showed that some participants were unfamiliar with key protection concepts and terminology and were unsure which channels to use for complaints or what steps to take when reporting exploitation. The session highlighted the need for continued awareness activities on protection and reporting at the site.

Results/
Participants engaged with the facilitator by asking questions and sharing feedback. The discussion clarified which channels to use to inquire about assistance and services, submit feedback or a complaint, or report exploitation confidentially.

Primary Activity: Two-Way Information Sharing, Feedback and Complaints
Topic(s): PSEA (Protection against Sexual Exploitation & Abuse), General Protection
Summary:
An awareness session on Protection, Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA), and Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP) was held at Al-Musbah Site (DEB2499) on Monday, 9 November 2026, from 10:20 to 11:20 a.m. The session was attended by 21 displaced women living at the site.

Topics Covered

The session covered protection principles, including dignity and safety, and emphasized residents’ right to receive humanitarian assistance without being asked for payment or personal favors. Participants learned about their right to information, participation, and feedback. The facilitator used practical examples to explain how to submit complaints through official channels, how confidentiality and impartiality apply when handling complaints, and how monitoring and evaluation use community feedback to assess service quality.

Challenges

Some participants were unfamiliar with organizations’ official complaints channels and the steps for submitting a complaint. There was also limited awareness of how confidentiality and privacy are protected when reporting sensitive concerns. The discussion highlighted the need for further awareness sessions on these topics.

Results

Participants gained a clearer understanding of which official channels to use and how to submit a complaint. The session also reinforced the importance of reporting exploitation, abuse, or attempted extortion through official channels and seeking support confidentially.

Primary Activity: Two-Way Information Sharing, Feedback and Complaints
Topic(s): PSEA (Protection against Sexual Exploitation & Abuse), General Protection
Summary:
An awareness session on protection, Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA), and Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP) was held at Al-Noor Site (DEB4740) on Monday, 9 November 2026, from 12:30 to 1:30 p.m. The session was attended by 23 displaced women living at the site.

Topics Covered

The session covered dignity, non-discrimination, confidentiality, and safe access to humanitarian assistance and support services. Participants discussed their right to receive assistance free of charge and without being asked for favors. The session also explained how to contact service providers through official channels, submit complaints and feedback, and safely report sexual exploitation, abuse, or coercion. It addressed residents’ right to information and participation, and how monitoring and follow-up help organizations respond to concerns about services.

Challenges

Some participants were unsure which organizations to contact, how to submit a complaint confidentially, or what steps to take if they experienced exploitation, abuse, or coercion. The discussions also revealed uncertainty about residents’ rights and responsibilities and how organizations follow up on concerns. Fear that sensitive information might be disclosed made some participants hesitant to report incidents.

Results

Participants gained a clearer understanding of which official channels to use to contact service providers, seek assistance, and submit complaints confidentially. The session clarified what steps to take when facing exploitation, abuse, or coercion and reinforced that humanitarian assistance is provided free of charge.

Primary Activity: Two-Way Information Sharing, Feedback and Complaints
Topic(s): PSEA (Protection against Sexual Exploitation & Abuse), General Protection
Summary:
An awareness session on protection, Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA), and Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP) was held at Nablus Site (DEB4948) on Monday, 9 November 2026, from 2:00 to 3:00 p.m.The session was attended by displaced women living at the site.

Topics Covered

The session covered dignity, non-discrimination, confidentiality, and access to support services. It explained what constitutes sexual exploitation and abuse and how to report suspected misconduct safely. The facilitator also discussed residents’ rights to information and participation in decisions affecting the site, how to raise priority needs with site management, and how to submit complaints and feedback through official channels, including those of Faris Al-Arab and the Sanad Network. The session highlighted how monitoring and community feedback support accountability.

Challenges

Some participants were unsure about their roles and responsibilities at the site, how to communicate priority needs to site management, or how to participate in decisions affecting services. The notes also identified limited familiarity with PSEA terminology, the appropriate channels for reporting sexual exploitation and abuse, and how to submit a complaint confidentially.

Results

Participants gained a clearer understanding of when and how to submit a complaint and which official channels to use. The session reinforced the importance of contacting the responsible organization, protecting privacy when reporting sensitive concerns, and helping residents affected by abuse reach appropriate support.

Topic: Site Management Committee Establishment, Coordination or Planning
Summary:
On Monday, 9 November 2026, the NRC team, represented by Hussein Ali, held a community meeting at the AlYaqeen site with the site management and community committees. The meeting introduced the upcoming Cash for Work activity, explained how workers will be selected, and clarified the tasks they will carry out at the site.

The team began by describing the CfW activity, its objectives and the kinds of work the selected workers will do. Site management was then asked to nominate 20 workers from the site, spread across its blocks so that representation is fair. The team explained the agreed selection criteria to the management and committees so that nominations would follow them.

The team also explained the selection process. Each nominee will complete an application using a selection questionnaire. Final selection will follow the agreed criteria, with priority for the most vulnerable and those most in need.

The meeting closed with agreed next steps. Site management will send the names of the 20 nominees, listed by block. The NRC team will then complete the questionnaires with them and finalize the selection. Photos from the meeting are attached to the report.

Topic: Site Management Committee Establishment, Coordination or Planning
Summary:
On Monday, 10 November 2026, Hussein Ali and Abdullah AlKurdi visited the AlJundi AlMajhoul site to assess damage from the recent winter storm. The visit had two goals: to follow up on the planned sewage and drainage network, and to check the condition of the existing tents.

The team confirmed that sewage pipes and manholes will be provided at the site, with one manhole every 10 metres to drain both wastewater and rainwater. Residents will be responsible for connecting the pipes from their tents and shelters to these manholes. The site manager is encouraging organisations to help displaced families complete these connections.

The team also found that many tents are leaking through the roof and sides, so they need to be replaced or reinforced with tarpaulin sheeting. The urgent needs identified were:

support from organisations to connect tents and shelters to the drainage network
replacement tents for those that are badly damaged
tarpaulin sheeting to reinforce leaking tents
These measures are needed to protect residents from further weather-related damage as winter continues.

Topic: Site Management Committee Establishment, Coordination or Planning
Summary:
On Monday, 10 November 2026, Hussein Ali and Abdullah AlKurdi visited the site to assess damage from the recent heavy rainfall.

Cause: The site sits below street level, so rainwater ran in from the street and pooled between the tents.
During the storm: Water got into tents and shelters from the first night through the following day. There was no equipment on site to deal with it, which made things worse.
Damage: 12 families' shelters were completely destroyed. Several tent roofs were damaged and there were no tarpaulins to stop the leaks. Mattresses and blankets were soaked because there was no plastic sheeting to cover them.
Urgent needs:

Summary:
On Monday, 9 November 2026, Hussein Ali of the NRC team met with the AlEkhwa site management and committees. The meeting introduced the upcoming Cash for Work (CfW) activity, explained how workers will be selected, and clarified the work they will do at the site.

The team began by explaining the activity's objectives and the tasks the selected workers will carry out. The team explained the agreed selection criteria to management and the committees, and stressed that all nominations must follow them.

Each of the 20 nominees will complete an application using a selection questionnaire. Final selection will be based on the agreed criteria, with priority given to the most vulnerable and those most in need.

The meeting ended with two next steps. Site management will submit the names of the 20 nominees, grouped by block. The NRC team will then complete the questionnaire with each nominee and finalize the selection against the criteria. Photos from the visit are attached to the meeting record.

Summary: On 9 September 2026, a meeting was held with the Site Management Committee at Ewaa Al Jalees Site (Site Code: DEB2355), Al-Masha’la, Deir al-Balah Governorate, under the Inclusive Site Management and Protection for Displaced Communities in the Gaza Strip project (OCHA, Project Code OCHG0AW). The meeting explained the Cash for Work (CFW) opportunity, the nomination criteria, and the committee’s role in nominating candidates from the site population. The committee agreed to nominate five persons who meet the criteria, with their data to be submitted for review and verification before final selection.

Topic: Site Management Committee Establishment, Coordination or Planning
Summary: On 9 September 2026, a meeting was held with the Site Management Committee at Ewaa Al Jalees Site (Site Code: DEB2355), Al-Masha’la, Deir al-Balah Governorate, under the Inclusive Site Management and Protection for Displaced Communities in the Gaza Strip project (OCHA, Project Code OCHG0AW). The meeting identified the site’s main needs and challenges and agreed priority interventions to improve safety and living conditions, with a focus on night-time movement of children, older persons, and persons with disabilities. Priorities were ranked as: (1) improved lighting in public areas and pathways, (2) securing hazardous pits linked to sanitation, (3) improved pathways, (4) safety and emergency supplies, and (5) a multi-purpose space.

Summary: On 29 September 2026, a hygiene and safe water awareness session was conducted at Nazihi Alshamal Site (Site Code: DEB4779), Deir al-Balah Governorate, under the Inclusive Site Management and Protection for Displaced Communities in the Gaza Strip project (OCHA, Project Code OCHG0AW). The session was implemented in coordination with UNICEF, with Dr. Ibrahim Al-Habbash as the facilitator. It covered keeping water and water storage containers clean, simple practices families can apply in displacement conditions, and proper water handling within the household. The Site Management Committee facilitated access to the site and organized participation.

Primary Activity: Two-Way Information Sharing, Feedback and Complaints
Summary: The awareness session covered key protection concepts and principles, including the distinction between exploitation, abuse, and harassment. Participants were also informed about safe and available reporting mechanisms. In addition, a humanitarian organizations contact directory was distributed to help participants access relevant services, support, complaint, and reporting channels.

Summary: On 28 September 2026, a protection awareness session for women was conducted at Nazihi Alshamal Site (Site Code: DEB4779), Deir al-Balah Governorate, under the Inclusive Site Management and Protection for Displaced Communities in the Gaza Strip project (OCHA, Project Code OCHG0AW). The session was implemented by protection responders from Fares Al-Arab Foundation, hosted at the site through the Site Management Committee. It provided protection awareness and gave women space to express their needs and the challenges they face in displacement, and discussed ways of coping with and recovering from them.
